idea.description: Test an explicitly balanced mixture of uniform random-prefix terminal-mask examples and baseline random-mask examples within the supplied corrected BERT4Rec. Separate loss-normalization effects from masking effects before attributing any gain. Train exactly one independent model per category and retain appended-mask inference.
idea.motivation: Terminal examples remove the future context available in interior reconstruction and align supervision with prediction. This may reduce two user-facing failures: treating older interests as continuing demand and ranking weak, broadly related matches above choices supported by the immediate context. These are hypotheses rather than demonstrated remedies: uniform original-position sampling does not explicitly favor recent events, and histories alone cannot establish ownership, compatibility, or incremental usefulness. Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics show weaker training-exposed margins, motivating a test of endpoint ranking, but their margins do not establish the mechanism or held-out improvement.
idea.implementation_notes:
Start from the supplied corrected BERT4Rec without inspecting other trials or reusing their checkpoints. Preserve the baseline architecture, loss function, negative count and distribution, optimizer, user-sampling distribution, initialization seed, and update count. Define the experiment as endpoint alignment rather than recency weighting.

Normalization control: determine the supplied baseline's actual reduction from its provided code. If it averages all supervised tokens together, first compare that baseline with per-example averaging using identical sampled histories, corrupted inputs, targets, negatives, and update schedule. These are separate single-model trials, never fused. The primary masking comparison must use the same per-example reduction in control and treatment. For the treatment, construct equal-sized terminal and random branches and use loss = 0.5 * mean(terminal example losses) + 0.5 * mean(random example losses). Each example loss is the mean over its valid supervised positions. With an odd batch size, use a declared seeded alternating allocation and separate branch means. Equal coefficients do not imply equal gradient norms. Do not silently change normalization and attribute the entire difference to terminal masking.

For terminal examples, sample a cutoff j uniformly from 1 through len(history)-1 using zero-based indexing, requiring at least one preceding interaction. The target is history[j]; retain history[max(0,j-(L-1)):j], append the reserved MASK, and left-pad to L. Never include the target event or any later event. Earlier occurrences of the same item remain valid historical context. Random-mask examples retain corrected baseline corruption with supervised targets hidden; ensure every example has at least one valid supervised target. Use the same eligible user distribution in the normalization-matched comparison, explicitly reporting any exclusions required by histories shorter than two events. Continue the baseline negative sampler and its existing exclusions unchanged; document their exact behavior rather than silently introducing full-history exclusions or a different proposal.

The primary mixture also changes available context and supervised-target count, so it cannot isolate target placement alone. Record branch example counts, supervised-target counts, original cutoffs, retained/visible context lengths, corruption counts, and optional sampled branch gradient norms. Record provenance separately without changing the loader's (None, sequence, positive, negative) contract. If budget permits, a separate one-target control compares terminal-only, exactly-one-random-mask, and their mixture using matched user and pre-corruption sequence-length distributions; future-context availability remains an intentional treatment difference. Further controls can hold corrupted inputs fixed and supervise either all masked positions or one uniformly selected mask: with per-example normalization their expected gradients agree, but variance differs. A separate one-mask-versus-multiple-mask comparison with one supervised target measures corruption effects. Target-budget matching is an additional experiment, not interchangeable with the required fixed-update comparison. Defer recency-weighted endpoints, positional biases, and negative-hardness changes until endpoint alignment is assessed.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, exactly 200 batches per epoch, and at most 200 epochs. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; save artifacts beneath the trial directory. Execute single-GPU within the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget. Predeclare the 50% mixture, comparisons, and unchanged host-compatible checkpoint-selection rule before observing their validation outcomes. Each trial trains one model per category; prediction loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category, without averaging, independently fitted auxiliary scores, or fusion.

Preserve ModelView, log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Retain the four-tuple diagnostic loader and return measured metrics with definitions. Distinguish terminal and interior training margins when provenance is available; otherwise mark that distinction unavailable. Training-exposed margins and omitted history-sensitivity results cannot establish held-out gains or a preferred recency direction. Embedding alignment near 0.5 alone does not establish collapse or representation quality. Sampler provenance, fresh-process predictor parity, and attention-deletion checks remain unavailable until genuinely implemented and measured. Preserve existing diagnostic fixtures and add provenance or parity checks only through supported interfaces.

The embedded predictor writer must reproduce the trained architecture, ID mapping, category routing, reserved token IDs, and appended-mask construction. Truncate history to L-1 before appending MASK. Find the last nonpadding position from actual indices, never count-1. A fresh-process reload and score comparison is needed before claiming checkpoint/predictor parity; live-model checks alone are insufficient. Restrict information to public histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps. Do not use unavailable ratings, review text, item categories/prices/stores, simulator traits, held-out target timestamps, or test files.

Label the host metric sampled HR@10: one positive plus 99 unique negatives, 200 validation users/category, evaluation seed 42. Report each category's hits/200 and HR@10, its difference from baseline, and the equally weighted macro difference. One extra hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. If the host supplies paired user-level outcomes, compute a category-stratified paired bootstrap with 10,000 resamples and analysis seed 42, resampling 200 user pairs within each category while retaining fixed candidate outcomes; report the percentile 95% interval for the macro difference. If those outcomes are unavailable, report the interval as unavailable rather than reconstructing or inventing it. Intervals condition on fitted models, categories, and candidates and exclude training-seed variability, candidate-sampling variability, and adaptive selection. Disclose all trials, checkpoint evaluations, budget use, baseline/selected configurations, and selection rule. Treat validation findings as exploratory and freeze selection before the host's untouched final evaluation. Do not interpret sampled gains as full-catalog gains or infer generalization across seeds or domains.

# === main_code.py ===
"""Per-dataset BERT4Rec baseline for Amazon Reviews.

Trains one independent BERT4Rec checkpoint per dataset while sharing one default
hyper-parameter profile across datasets. The generated predict.py routes by the
optional dataset_name keyword used by the RecHarness Amazon Reviews harness.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
import os
import pickle
import random
from collections import defaultdict

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

DEFAULT_DATASETS = [
    "Movies_and_TV",
    "Industrial_and_Scientific",
    "Electronics",
    "CDs_and_Vinyl",
]
DATASETS = [
    part.strip()
    for part in os.environ.get("GAGC_DATASETS", ",".join(DEFAULT_DATASETS)).split(",")
    if part.strip()
]

### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Required data boundary and fixed training seed
DATA_DIR = os.environ["GAGC_DATA_DIR"]

SEED = 42
### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
random.seed(SEED)
np.random.seed(SEED)
torch.manual_seed(SEED)
if torch.cuda.is_available():
    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(SEED)


def _read_split(path: str) -> dict[int, list[int]]:
    data: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return {}
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            parts = line.strip().split()
            if len(parts) == 2:
                data[int(parts[0])].append(int(parts[1]))
    return dict(data)


def _load_itemnum(data_dir: str, dataset_name: str) -> int:
    stats_path = os.path.join(data_dir, "dataset_stats.json")
    if os.path.isfile(stats_path):
        with open(stats_path) as f:
            stats = json.load(f)
        if dataset_name in stats:
            return int(stats[dataset_name]["itemnum"])
    itemnum = 0
    for split in ("train", "valid"):
        path = os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_{split}.txt")
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            for line in f:
                parts = line.strip().split()
                if len(parts) == 2:
                    itemnum = max(itemnum, int(parts[1]))
    return itemnum


def load_dataset(dataset_name: str, data_dir: str):
    user_train = _read_split(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_train.txt"))
    user_valid = _read_split(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_valid.txt"))
    itemnum = _load_itemnum(data_dir, dataset_name)
    return user_train, user_valid, itemnum


### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Balanced uniform-prefix terminal masking with explicit normalization controls
# Each invocation trains one configuration and one model per category.
# Default treatment: exactly half terminal examples, per-example BPR.
# Matched masking control: BERT4REC_MASKING=random, reduction=per_example.
# Normalization control: BERT4REC_MASKING=random, reduction=token.
# The two random controls use identical sampling code and random draws.
# Checkpoint selection remains first strict improvement in validation HR@10.
MASKING_MODE = os.environ.get("BERT4REC_MASKING", "mixture")
LOSS_REDUCTION = os.environ.get("BERT4REC_LOSS_REDUCTION", "per_example")
RECONSTRUCTION_MASK_PROBABILITY = 0.15
if MASKING_MODE not in {"mixture", "random"}:
    raise ValueError("BERT4REC_MASKING must be mixture or random")
if LOSS_REDUCTION not in {"per_example", "token"}:
    raise ValueError("BERT4REC_LOSS_REDUCTION must be per_example or token")
if MASKING_MODE == "mixture" and LOSS_REDUCTION != "per_example":
    raise ValueError("The balanced mixture requires per-example normalization")


def sample_batch(
    user_train: dict[int, list[int]], itemnum: int, batch_size: int, maxlen: int
):
    if maxlen < 2 or batch_size < 1:
        raise ValueError("maxlen must be at least two and batch_size positive")
    if MASKING_MODE == "mixture" and batch_size < 2:
        raise ValueError("The balanced mixture requires batch_size >= 2")
    users = [u for u, items in user_train.items() if len(items) >= 2]
    if not users:
        raise RuntimeError("no users with at least two training interactions")
    # Alternate the larger branch for odd batches; never infer branch identity
    # from target counts, since random masking can also select a single target.
    call_index = getattr(sample_batch, "call_index", 0)
    terminal_count = 0
    if MASKING_MODE == "mixture":
        terminal_count = batch_size // 2 + (batch_size % 2) * (call_index % 2)
    sample_batch.call_index = call_index + 1
    sample_batch.last_terminal_count = terminal_count
    batch_seq, batch_pos, batch_neg, provenance = [], [], [], []
    for row in range(batch_size):
        user = random.choice(users)
        history = user_train[user]
        terminal = row < terminal_count
        if terminal:
            endpoint = random.randint(1, len(history) - 1)
            start = max(0, endpoint - (maxlen - 1))
            # Target and all later events are absent from the input context.
            items = history[start:endpoint] + [history[endpoint]]
        else:
            endpoint = len(history) - 1
            start = max(0, len(history) - maxlen)
            # Random reconstruction uses the complete retained training window,
            # without the previous recency-weighted prefix selection.
            items = history[start:]
        seq = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        pos = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        neg = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        seq[-len(items) :] = items
        offset = maxlen - len(items)
        eligible = list(range(offset, maxlen))
        if terminal:
            selected = [maxlen - 1]
        else:
            selected = [
                i for i in eligible if random.random() < RECONSTRUCTION_MASK_PROBABILITY
            ]
            if not selected:
                selected = [random.choice(eligible)]
        # Preserve rejection sampling of one uniform catalog negative per target,
        # excluding every item in this user's full supplied training history.
        interacted = set(history)
        if len(interacted) >= itemnum:
            raise RuntimeError("no unobserved negative item available")
        for i in selected:
            pos[i] = seq[i]
            seq[i] = itemnum + 1
            item = random.randint(1, itemnum)
            while item in interacted:
                item = random.randint(1, itemnum)
            neg[i] = item
        branch = "terminal" if terminal else "random"
        provenance.append(
            {
                "user": int(user),
                "branch": branch,
                "cutoff": endpoint,
                "target_positions": [start + i - offset for i in selected],
                "retained_length": len(items),
                "visible_context_length": len(items) - len(selected),
                "corruption_count": len(selected),
            }
        )
        stats = sample_batch.epoch_stats.setdefault(
            branch,
            {
                "examples": 0,
                "targets": 0,
                "cutoff_sum": 0,
                "retained_length_sum": 0,
                "visible_context_length_sum": 0,
                "corruption_count": 0,
            },
        )
        stats["examples"] += 1
        stats["targets"] += len(selected)
        stats["cutoff_sum"] += endpoint
        stats["retained_length_sum"] += len(items)
        stats["visible_context_length_sum"] += len(items) - len(selected)
        stats["corruption_count"] += len(selected)
        batch_seq.append(seq)
        batch_pos.append(pos)
        batch_neg.append(neg)
    # Side-channel provenance preserves the three-array sampler and four-tuple
    # diagnostic-loader interfaces. Only the latest batch is retained in memory.
    sample_batch.last_provenance = provenance
    return np.asarray(batch_seq), np.asarray(batch_pos), np.asarray(batch_neg)


sample_batch.epoch_stats = {}
### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END


def _history_to_tensor(
    history: list[int], maxlen: int, device: torch.device
) -> torch.Tensor:
    seq_arr = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    for i, item in enumerate(reversed(history[-maxlen:])):
        seq_arr[maxlen - 1 - i] = item
    return torch.tensor([seq_arr], dtype=torch.long, device=device)


def evaluate_val(
    model: nn.Module,
    user_train: dict[int, list[int]],
    user_valid: dict[int, list[int]],
    itemnum: int,
    device: torch.device,
    maxlen: int,
    num_users: int = 200,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Reproducible validation without consuming training randomness
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    val_users = [u for u in user_valid if u in user_train and user_valid[u]]
    if len(val_users) > num_users:
        val_users = rng.sample(val_users, num_users)
    ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
    if not val_users:
        return {"HR@10": 0.0, "HR@20": 0.0, "NDCG@10": 0.0, "NDCG@20": 0.0}

    hr10 = hr20 = ndcg10 = ndcg20 = 0.0
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for user in val_users:
            target = user_valid[user][0]
            history = user_train[user]
            interacted = set(history) | {target, 0}
            ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Fixed unique validation negatives with bounded sampling
            available_count = itemnum - sum(1 <= item <= itemnum for item in interacted)
            if available_count < 99:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"validation user {user} has only {available_count} eligible negatives; "
                    "99 unique negatives are required"
                )
            candidates = [target]
            if available_count < 198:
                available = [
                    item for item in range(1, itemnum + 1) if item not in interacted
                ]
                candidates.extend(rng.sample(available, 99))
            else:
                while len(candidates) < 100:
                    neg_item = rng.randint(1, itemnum)
                    if neg_item not in interacted:
                        interacted.add(neg_item)
                        candidates.append(neg_item)
            ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
            seq_t = _history_to_tensor(history, maxlen, device)
            cand_t = torch.tensor(candidates, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
            scores = model.score_candidates(seq_t, cand_t).detach().cpu().tolist()
            rank = sorted(range(len(scores)), key=lambda i: -scores[i]).index(0)
            hr10 += 1.0 if rank < 10 else 0.0
            hr20 += 1.0 if rank < 20 else 0.0
            ndcg10 += (1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)) if rank < 10 else 0.0
            ndcg20 += (1.0 / math.log2(rank + 2)) if rank < 20 else 0.0
    n = float(len(val_users))
    model.train()
    return {
        "HR@10": hr10 / n,
        "HR@20": hr20 / n,
        "NDCG@10": ndcg10 / n,
        "NDCG@20": ndcg20 / n,
    }


### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Implement normalization controls and explicit balanced-branch BPR
def bpr_sequence_loss(
    model: nn.Module,
    seq: torch.Tensor,
    pos: torch.Tensor,
    neg: torch.Tensor,
    terminal_count: int | None = None,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    # Branch membership is supplied by the training caller, never inferred
    # from target counts or mutable sampler state inside this function.
    # Diagnostic callers may omit it to obtain ordinary per-example BPR.
    if terminal_count is not None:
        if not 0 <= terminal_count < pos.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError("terminal_count must leave at least one random example")

class BERT4RecModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(
        self,
        itemnum: int,
        hidden_units: int = 64,
        num_blocks: int = 2,
        num_heads: int = 2,
        dropout_rate: float = 0.2,
        maxlen: int = 128,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.itemnum = itemnum
        self.hidden_units = hidden_units
        self.maxlen = maxlen
        self.mask_token = itemnum + 1
        self.item_emb = nn.Embedding(itemnum + 2, hidden_units, padding_idx=0)
        self.pos_emb = nn.Embedding(maxlen + 1, hidden_units, padding_idx=0)
        encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=hidden_units,
            nhead=num_heads,
            dim_feedforward=hidden_units * 4,
            dropout=dropout_rate,
            activation="gelu",
            batch_first=True,
            norm_first=True,
        )
        self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_layers=num_blocks)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        with torch.no_grad():
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.item_emb.weight)
            self.item_emb.weight[0].zero_()
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.pos_emb.weight)
            self.pos_emb.weight[0].zero_()

    def encode_sequence(self, seq: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        batch, length = seq.shape
        pos = torch.arange(length, device=seq.device).unsqueeze(0).expand(batch, -1) + 1
        pos = pos * (seq != 0).long()
        x = self.item_emb(seq) * (self.hidden_units**0.5) + self.pos_emb(pos)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        padding = seq == 0
        safe_padding = padding.clone()
        safe_padding[padding.all(dim=1), -1] = False
        x = self.encoder(x, src_key_padding_mask=safe_padding)
        return self.norm(x)

    def forward(self, seq: torch.Tensor, pos: torch.Tensor, neg: torch.Tensor):
        out = self.encode_sequence(seq)
        pos_scores = (out * self.item_emb(pos)).sum(dim=-1)
        neg_scores = (out * self.item_emb(neg)).sum(dim=-1)
        return pos_scores, neg_scores

    def score_candidates(
        self, seq: torch.Tensor, candidates: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        prediction_seq = torch.zeros_like(seq)
        prediction_seq[:, :-1] = seq[:, 1:]
        prediction_seq[:, -1] = self.mask_token
        out = self.encode_sequence(prediction_seq)
        user_emb = out[0, -1]
        cand_emb = self.item_emb(candidates)
        return torch.matmul(cand_emb, user_emb)

    def _pack_inference(self, history):
        length = int(self.network.maxlen)
        if length < 1:
            raise ValueError("BERT4Rec maxlen must be positive")
        retained = list(history)[-(length - 1) :] if length > 1 else []
        tokens = retained + [int(self.network.mask_token)]
        return [0] * (length - len(tokens)) + tokens

    def _integrity(self):
        model = self.network
        length, itemnum = int(model.maxlen), int(model.itemnum)
        result = {
            "sampler_provenance": None,
            "sampler_provenance_reason": (
                "The loader supplies corrupted inputs and labels, but no original "
                "event/position provenance. Same-position labels, corruption branches "
                "and loss weights cannot be independently certified."
            ),
            "fresh_process_predictor_parity": None,
            "fresh_process_predictor_parity_reason": (
                "No fresh-process predictor/checkpoint runner is supplied through ModelView. "
                "Live inference checks below do not establish checkpoint, mapping or writer parity."
            ),
            "attention_deletion": None,
            "attention_deletion_reason": (
                "The supplied encode_sequence interface has no diagnostic key/value mask hook."
            ),
        }
        if itemnum < 1 or length < 1:
            result["failure"] = "Invalid item vocabulary or sequence length"
            return result
        other = min(2, itemnum)
        histories = [[], [1], [1] * length, [1, other, 1]]
        raw = torch.zeros((4, length), dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)
        for row, history in enumerate(histories):
            retained = history[-length:]
            if retained:
                raw[row, -len(retained) :] = torch.tensor(retained, device=self.device)
        expected = torch.tensor(
            [self._pack_inference(h) for h in histories],
            dtype=torch.long,
            device=self.device,
        )
        shifted = torch.zeros_like(raw)
        shifted[:, :-1] = raw[:, 1:]
        shifted[:, -1] = model.mask_token
        candidates = torch.arange(1, min(itemnum, 32) + 1, device=self.device)
        # Match the live single-user batch shape to avoid attributing differences
        # between batched kernels to preprocessing or checkpoint inconsistency.
        reference = torch.stack(
            [
                model.encode_sequence(expected[i : i + 1])[0, -1]
                @ model.item_emb(candidates).T
                for i in range(4)
            ]
        )
        observed_inputs = []

        def capture_sequence(module, args):
            tokens = args[0]
            if tokens.ndim == 2 and tuple(tokens.shape) == (1, length):
                observed_inputs.append(tokens.detach().clone())

        handle = model.item_emb.register_forward_pre_hook(capture_sequence)
        try:
            live = torch.stack(
                [model.score_candidates(raw[i : i + 1], candidates) for i in range(4)]
            )
        finally:
            handle.remove()
        ids_match = len(observed_inputs) == 4 and all(
            torch.equal(observed_inputs[i], expected[i : i + 1]) for i in range(4)
        )
        finite = bool(torch.isfinite(reference).all() & torch.isfinite(live).all())
        result.update(
            {
                "reserved_mask_id_valid": int(model.mask_token) == itemnum + 1,
                "fixture_count": 4,
                "fixture_names": ["empty", "short", "full_length", "repeated_id"],
                "inference_ids_match": bool(ids_match),
                "constructed_shift_ids_match": bool(torch.equal(expected, shifted)),
                "observed_sequence_calls": len(observed_inputs),
                "readout_absolute_index": length - 1,
                "finite_scores": finite,
                "live_inference_allclose": finite
                and bool(torch.allclose(reference, live, rtol=1.3e-6, atol=1e-5)),
                "live_inference_max_abs_error": (
                    float((reference - live).abs().max()) if finite else None
                ),
                "rtol": 1.3e-6,
                "atol": 1e-5,
            }
        )
        # A synthetic provenance control rejects shifted labels by position,
        # even when repeated IDs make their item identities indistinguishable.
        selected = np.array([False, True, False])
        source_positions = np.arange(3)
        correct = source_positions.copy()
        shifted_labels = np.array([1, 2, 2])
        result["shifted_provenance_control_rejected"] = bool(
            np.array_equal(correct[selected], source_positions[selected])
            and not np.array_equal(shifted_labels[selected], source_positions[selected])
        )
        result["shifted_provenance_control_scope"] = (
            "Synthetic validator only; not sampler certification"
        )
        if length < 3:
            result["padding_and_bidirectionality_reason"] = (
                "Fixtures require maxlen >= 3"
            )
            return result
        fixture = torch.tensor(
            [self._pack_inference([1])], dtype=torch.long, device=self.device
        )
        original = model.encode_sequence(fixture)
        saved_padding = model.item_emb.weight[0].detach().clone()
        try:
            model.item_emb.weight[0].copy_(
                saved_padding
                + torch.arange(
                    model.hidden_units,
                    device=self.device,
                    dtype=saved_padding.dtype,
                )
                + 1
            )
            perturbed = model.encode_sequence(fixture)
        finally:
            model.item_emb.weight[0].copy_(saved_padding)
        valid = fixture != 0
        result["padding_embedding_invariant"] = bool(
            torch.allclose(original[valid], perturbed[valid], rtol=1.3e-6, atol=1e-5)
        )
        result["padding_max_abs_error"] = float(
            (original[valid] - perturbed[valid]).abs().max()
        )
        # Perturb a visible token right of an interior query. A causal encoder
        # cannot pass this influence check; degeneracy is reported as inconclusive.
        changed = fixture.clone()
        changed[:, -1] = 1
        changed_features = model.encode_sequence(changed)
        right_delta = float((original[:, -2] - changed_features[:, -2]).abs().max())
        result["right_context_max_abs_influence"] = right_delta
        result["right_context_influence_detected"] = right_delta > 1e-5
        result["right_context_scope"] = (
            "Observed right-token influence; zero influence is inconclusive or a structural failure"
        )
        omitted = fixture.clone()
        omitted[:, -1] = 0
        omitted_scores = (
            model.encode_sequence(omitted)[:, -1] @ model.item_emb(candidates).T
        )
        wrong_index = int((fixture[0] != 0).sum()) - 1
        wrong_scores = original[:, wrong_index] @ model.item_emb(candidates).T
        result["omitted_mask_control_rejected"] = not bool(
            torch.allclose(
                omitted_scores,
                original[:, -1] @ model.item_emb(candidates).T,
                rtol=1.3e-6,
                atol=1e-5,
            )
        )
        result["count_minus_one_control_rejected"] = (
            not bool(
                torch.allclose(
                    wrong_scores,
                    original[:, -1] @ model.item_emb(candidates).T,
                    rtol=1.3e-6,
                    atol=1e-5,
                )
            )
            if wrong_index != length - 1
            else None
        )
        return result

    @staticmethod
    def _summary(values):
        values = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64)
        if values.size == 0:
            return {
                "mean": None,
                "count": 0,
                "ci95": None,
                "reason": "No eligible user observations",
            }
        if not np.isfinite(values).all():
            raise ValueError("Nonfinite observations in diagnostic bootstrap")
        rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
        indices = rng.integers(0, values.size, size=(1000, values.size))
        means = values[indices].mean(axis=1)
        return {
            "mean": float(values.mean()),
            "count": int(values.size),
            "ci95": np.quantile(means, [0.025, 0.975]).tolist(),
            "reason": None,
        }

    def _history_sensitivity(self):
        histories = self.user_train.get("History", self.user_train)
        itemnum = int(self.network.itemnum)
        length = int(self.network.maxlen)
        eligible = []
        popularity = Counter()
        for user, events in histories.items():
            events = list(events)
            if any(int(x) < 1 or int(x) > itemnum for x in events):
                raise ValueError("Training history contains a noncatalog item ID")
            events = [int(x) for x in events]
            popularity.update(events)
            # One last training event per user; all later events are absent.
            prefix = events[:-1][-(length - 1) :] if length > 1 else []
            if len(prefix) >= 2:
                eligible.append((user, events, prefix, events[-1]))
        eligible.sort(key=lambda row: str(row[0]))
        if len(eligible) > 200:
            eligible = random.Random(42).sample(eligible, 200)
        length_cuts = (
            np.quantile([len(row[2]) for row in eligible], [0.25, 0.5, 0.75]).tolist()
            if eligible
            else []
        )
        pop_cuts = (
            np.quantile(
                [popularity[i] for i in range(1, itemnum + 1)], [0.25, 0.5, 0.75]
            ).tolist()
            if itemnum
            else []
        )
        rows = {seed: [] for seed in (42, 43, 44)}
        names = [
            "original",
            "compact_oldest",
            "compact_newest",
            "mask_oldest",
            "mask_newest",
        ]
        for user, events, prefix, target in eligible:
            k = min(3, len(prefix) // 2)
            base = self._pack_inference(prefix)
            old_mask, new_mask = base.copy(), base.copy()
            first = length - 1 - len(prefix)
            old_mask[first : first + k] = [self.network.mask_token] * k
            new_mask[length - 1 - k : length - 1] = [self.network.mask_token] * k
            inputs = [
                base,
                self._pack_inference(prefix[k:]),
                self._pack_inference(prefix[:-k]),
                old_mask,
                new_mask,
            ]
            seq = torch.tensor(inputs, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)
            features = self.network.encode_sequence(seq)[:, -1]
            excluded = set(events) | {0, target, int(self.network.mask_token)}
            available_count = itemnum - sum(1 <= x <= itemnum for x in excluded)
            for seed in (42, 43, 44):
                # Stable user-specific RNG; candidate sets are frozen for all interventions.
                rng = random.Random(f"{seed}:{user}")
                count = min(99, available_count)
                if available_count < 198:
                    pool = [x for x in range(1, itemnum + 1) if x not in excluded]
                    negatives = rng.sample(pool, count)
                else:
                    negatives, used = [], set()
                    while len(negatives) < count:
                        candidate = rng.randint(1, itemnum)
                        if candidate not in excluded and candidate not in used:
                            used.add(candidate)
                            negatives.append(candidate)
                candidates = torch.tensor([target] + negatives, device=self.device)
                scores = (
                    (features @ self.network.item_emb(candidates).T)
                    .float()
                    .cpu()
                    .numpy()
                )
                if not np.isfinite(scores).all():
                    raise ValueError("Nonfinite diagnostic candidate scores")
                measured, tops = {}, {}
                for index, name in enumerate(names):
                    order = np.argsort(-scores[index], kind="stable")
                    rank = int(np.flatnonzero(order == 0)[0]) + 1
                    tops[name] = set(order[:10].tolist())
                    measured[name] = {
                        "target_score": float(scores[index, 0]),
                        "rank": rank,
                        "hr10": float(rank <= 10),
                        "margin": (
                            float(scores[index, 0] - scores[index, 1:].max())
                            if count
                            else None
                        ),
                    }
                for name in names[1:]:
                    measured[name]["top10_overlap"] = len(
                        tops[name] & tops["original"]
                    ) / min(len(tops[name]), len(tops["original"]))
                    for metric in ("target_score", "rank", "hr10", "margin"):
                        value = measured[name][metric]
                        measured[name]["delta_" + metric] = (
                            value - measured["original"][metric]
                            if value is not None
                            else None
                        )
                for mode in ("compact", "mask"):
                    measured[mode + "_recent_minus_older"] = {
                        metric: (
                            (
                                measured[mode + "_newest"][metric]
                                - measured[mode + "_oldest"][metric]
                            )
                            if measured[mode + "_newest"][metric] is not None
                            else None
                        )
                        for metric in (
                            "target_score",
                            "rank",
                            "hr10",
                            "margin",
                            "top10_overlap",
                        )
                    }
                rows[seed].append(
                    {
                        "user": str(user),
                        "repeat": target in prefix,
                        "length_quartile": int(
                            np.searchsorted(length_cuts, len(prefix), side="right")
                        ),
                        "popularity_quartile": int(
                            np.searchsorted(pop_cuts, popularity[target], side="right")
                        ),
                        "candidate_count": count + 1,
                        "measurements": measured,
                    }
                )

        # Keep metric keys and explicit null summaries in empty strata.
        metric_keys = {
            name + "." + metric
            for records in rows.values()
            for record in records
            for name, measurements in record["measurements"].items()
            for metric in measurements
        }
        if not metric_keys:
            for name in names:
                metrics = ["target_score", "rank", "hr10", "margin"]
                if name != "original":
                    metrics += [
                        "top10_overlap",
                        "delta_target_score",
                        "delta_rank",
                        "delta_hr10",
                        "delta_margin",
                    ]
                metric_keys.update(name + "." + metric for metric in metrics)
            for mode in ("compact", "mask"):
                metric_keys.update(
                    mode + "_recent_minus_older." + metric
                    for metric in (
                        "target_score",
                        "rank",
                        "hr10",
                        "margin",
                        "top10_overlap",
                    )
                )

        def aggregate(records):
            output = {key: [] for key in sorted(metric_keys)}
            for record in records:
                for name, measurements in record["measurements"].items():
                    for metric, value in measurements.items():
                        if value is not None:
                            output[name + "." + metric].append(value)
            return {key: self._summary(values) for key, values in output.items()}

        draws = {}
        for seed, records in rows.items():
            draws[str(seed)] = {
                "users": len(records),
                "candidate_counts": dict(
                    Counter(r["candidate_count"] for r in records)
                ),
                "summary": aggregate(records),
                "repeat_explore": {
                    label: {
                        "users": sum(r["repeat"] == repeat for r in records),
                        "summary": aggregate(
                            [r for r in records if r["repeat"] == repeat]
                        ),
                    }
                    for label, repeat in (("repeat", True), ("explore", False))
                },
                "strata": {
                    field: {
                        str(q): {
                            "users": sum(r[field] == q for r in records),
                            "summary": aggregate([r for r in records if r[field] == q]),
                        }
                        for q in range(4)
                    }
                    for field in ("length_quartile", "popularity_quartile")
                },
            }
        return {
            "exposure": "training-exposed recovery; not held-out generalization",
            "category": getattr(self.view, "dataset_name", None),
            "eligible_selected_users": len(eligible),
            "reason": (
                None
                if eligible
                else "No training prefix with at least two retained items"
            ),
            "selection_seed": 42,
            "bootstrap_seed": 42,
            "bootstrap_resamples": 1000,
            "length_quartile_cutpoints": length_cuts,
            "item_training_popularity_quartile_cutpoints": pop_cuts,
            "candidate_policy": (
                "Positive exactly once; up to 99 unique catalog negatives excluding all "
                "permitted training-history items, positive, padding and mask. Frozen across interventions."
            ),
            "draws": draws,
            "category_metadata_breakdowns": {},
            "equal_category_macro": None,
            "equal_category_macro_reason": "A single ModelView cannot certify eligibility of all four categories",
        }

    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        modes = [(module, module.training) for module in self.network.modules()]
        python_rng = random.getstate()
        numpy_rng = np.random.get_state()
        cpu_rng = torch.get_rng_state()
        cuda_rng = torch.cuda.get_rng_state_all() if torch.cuda.is_available() else None
        try:
            self.network.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                integrity = self._integrity()
                collapse = self.analyze_embeddings_collapse_cosine(
                    sample_size=2048, seed=42
                )
                margins, breakdown = (
                    self.analyze_pos_neg_margin_with_category_breakdown(
                        train_loader, num_batches=10, eps=0.5, topk_categories=20
                    )
                )
                required_checks = (
                    "reserved_mask_id_valid",
                    "inference_ids_match",
                    "finite_scores",
                    "live_inference_allclose",
                    "padding_embedding_invariant",
                    "omitted_mask_control_rejected",
                    "count_minus_one_control_rejected",
                )
                failed_checks = [
                    key for key in required_checks if integrity.get(key) is False
                ]
                unavailable_checks = [
                    key for key in required_checks if integrity.get(key) is None
                ]

                    failed_checks.append("failure")
                # Invalid supervision is a structural failure, even when other
                # positions provide enough observations for finite margins.
                integrity["masked_target_alignment_valid"] = (
                    breakdown["invalid_target_positions"] == 0
                    if breakdown["inspected_batches"] > 0
                    else None

                if integrity["masked_target_alignment_valid"] is False:
                    failed_checks.append("masked_target_alignment_valid")
                elif integrity["masked_target_alignment_valid"] is None:
                    unavailable_checks.append("masked_target_alignment_valid")
                integrity["failed_required_checks"] = failed_checks
                integrity["unavailable_required_checks"] = unavailable_checks

                        "failed_checks": failed_checks,
                        "category_metadata_breakdowns": {},

                    if failed_checks

                metrics = {

                    "pos_neg_small_margin_rate": margins["small_margin_rate"],
                    "pos_neg_margin_sample_count": margins["count"],
                    "pos_neg_margin_reason": margins["reason"],
                    "pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown": breakdown,

                definitions = {
                    "bert4rec_integrity": (
                        "Independent appended-mask fixtures compare exact IDs and live candidate scores "

                    "pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate": "Fraction of valid masked targets with margin < 0",
                    "pos_neg_small_margin_rate": "Fraction of valid masked targets with margin < 0.5",
                    "pos_neg_margin_sample_count": "Number of valid supervised reserved-mask positions observed",
                    "pos_neg_margin_reason": "Reason no valid training margins were observed, or null",
                    "pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown": (
